title: Native C# Implementation
body: Native implementation of netcode.io in C#. Question, what language specification can we target? I think there are enough language features to warrant supporting C#7 at this point. Were you planning on supporting netcore, netstandard, or the full dotnetframework (or target against all of them). NET core 1.1, Net Standard 1.5 (eventually 2?) and NET 462.

nodes.body: I think the best language features to target would be those allow that people coding Unity 5.6 (latest release) to use netcode.io natively from inside Unity.
My understanding is that Unity is using Mono 4.4
Thanks! That was precisely the direction I was looking for.
https://forum.unity3d.com/threads/net-standard.451314/ Looks like Unity is looking to support netstandard 2 (whenever that is finally released)
Seems like for the current generation of Unity: "you'll need to stick to .NET 3.5 to be safe."

Maybe start with a basic implementation with .NET 3.5, and provide an upgraded version using more language features when as they become available in a widely released Unity version? 

From a game development point of view, Unity is the largest base of active C# users, so it would be ideal to support them, even if it means being limited to an older version of the language.

And I should apologize, I'm not super up to date with all the intricacies of C# versions and .NET so I don't really know all the details of this. My (very) limited exposure to the language is using Unity 5.6 and it definitely seems to be an older version of C#.

The biggest question I think is, is there a libsodium version for C# that is native, or support for the chachapoly natively in C#? Ideally, a pure C# version would be available, without dependencies on a DLL, but if that DLL is necessary, it's not the end of the world.
Oh and also, there is a C# wrapper for the API, which may be useful: https://github.com/RedpointGames/netcode.io
ps. Don't feel constrained to copy the C API, feel free to adapt your implementation to the best approach you see for the C# language.

Looks like the libsodium-net library is a net40 compliant wrapper which means we'll need to rely on Mono's support of 4.0 csproj projects. I don't see why that should be an issue as far as supporting Unity is concerned, although I understand the need to prefer a native implementation of libsodium in C#.

The dot net framework has undergone a significant change over the course of the last 12-18 months, starting with dnx and corefx, specifically netstandard and netcore for cross platform support. Prior to that you had to rely on platform specific PCLs which got the job done but were not unified. 

Thanks for the links to the wrapper, I'll use that as a reference moving forward. I agree - when implementing a library in a native language it's important to focus on idiomatic programming so that it doesn't look like C code ported to C#. This is especially important for consumers of the API / library, who will expect idioms similar to other .NET libraries that they have consumed in the past.

Unity 2017 now supports C#6 & .NET 4.6

What's the current status on this? I have some free time and I was thinking of adopting this as a side project.
The current status is that it's available for you to work on!

Can use any version of C# for implementation (e.g. C#7) just need to target the right version of [.NET Standard](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/blob/master/docs/versions.md) rather than the confusing mix of PCL versions,

Currently I think to get Unity, Xamarin.iOS/Mac/Android and UWP (Xbox, Win10) that would be a max of .NET Standard 1.4?
